log_destination.description: Where logs are written: 'syslog', 'stdout', or a file path.

listen_address.description: IP address the daemon listens on.

listen_port.description: TCP port for incoming connections (Postfix usually connects to this port for policy checks).

max_requests_per_worker.description: Maximum requests per worker before it's restarted (0 = unlimited).

timeout_connect.description: Timeout (in seconds) for upstream connections (e.g., to auth or lookup servers).

timeout_data.description: Timeout (in seconds) for processing a request body (e.g., from Postfix).

timeout_idle.description: Idle connection timeout (in seconds) for clients.

auth_enabled.description: Enable external authentication (e.g., for user-based rules).

auth_server.description: URI or socket path for the auth server (e.g., LDAP URL or PostgreSQL DSN).

default.name: reject_null_sender
default.description: Reject messages with null sender when not allowed
default.action: REJECT Sender address is null and null senders are not allowed

name.description: Unique identifier for the module (used in log messages and for referencing).

match.description: Postfix-style condition (e.g., 'sender = /example\.com/' or 'recipient = /@my\.com/') — may be empty if only default action is needed.

action.description: Postfix policy action to return: 'DUNNO', 'OK', 'REJECT <msg>', 'DISCARD', 'DEFER', etc.

use_cache.description: Enable Postfix smtpd_policy_cache integration (requires compatible Postfix version).

cache_path.description: Path to the policy cache directory (if caching is enabled).

cache_ttl.description: Time (in seconds) to cache policy decisions.

name.description: Unique name for the rate limit rule.

key.description: Key to track — e.g., 'client_address', 'sender', 'recipient', or composite like 'client_address+sender'.

rate.description: Max events per time unit (e.g., 5 per minute).

burst.description: Allowed burst (above rate) before limiting kicks in.
